data: simulated dataset: 50 shops, 5,000 customers, 91 days (2026-06-01 to 2026-08-30)

demand.name: Hourly customer demand
demand.target: customers arriving per shop per hour (08:00-20:59)
demand.split: time-based: first 80% of 91 dates train, last 20% test (from 2026-08-12); model chosen on a validation window starting 2026-07-28

model_selection_validation_mae.selection_rule: lowest validation MAE; prefer linear unless forest is >1% better

limitations: Trained on simulated data (Poisson arrivals); it learns the simulator's weekday and hour multipliers.
Most of the signal is the historical shop/hour/weekday average; the model adds little beyond it.
No seasonality or holidays: the data covers 91 summer days only.

waiting_time.name: Walk-in waiting time
waiting_time.split: time-based: first 80% of 91 dates train, last 20% test (from 2026-08-12)
limitations: Features describe the queue at the top of the hour, so they can be up to 59 minutes stale.
Errors are large for very long waits (heavy-tailed target); treat long estimates as ranges.
In the live demo the queue counts come from the live store, not from a sensor.

no_show.name: Appointment no-show risk
limitations: In the simulator the no-show label is assigned at random; the only learnable signal is that missed bookings were given uniformly random hours while completed ones follow peak hours.
Without the hour feature the model is no better than chance (see roc_auc_without_hour_feature).
Do not use it to charge deposits or penalise customers.
